balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

segmentProfit.title: Recurring underlying profit by segment
segmentProfit.content:
Swire Pacific is a conglomerate: this splits Recurring Underlying Profit across its six reporting segments — Property, Beverages, Cathay Pacific Group, HAECO & Others (aviation services), Trading & Industrial, and Head Office/Healthcare.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): this is the segment data the DCF's sum-of-the-parts model is built on — Property and Cathay are marked at market value of the listed stakes rather than DCF'd from this profit line, so compare the relative size of the slices, not just the dollar totals.

What to watch:

  • Head Office/Healthcare is a persistent drag (negative every year disclosed) — corporate costs and loss-making healthcare associates
  • Cathay Group's swing from recovery to a steadier run-rate
  • Only FY2023 onward is disclosed on this segment basis; no interim split

underlyingProfit.title: Underlying vs recurring underlying profit
underlyingProfit.content:
Underlying Profit is Swire's primary non-GAAP measure: statutory net income adjusted to exclude investment-property revaluation movements (and other items management treats as non-operating). Recurring Underlying Profit (disclosed FY2023+) goes further and also strips one-off disposal and revaluation-related gains that still sit inside Underlying Profit.

For Swire Pacific Limited ('B' shares): net income swings heavily on investment-property fair-value marks (see FY2020's loss); Underlying Profit is what management and the DCF's historical growth analysis actually track.

What to watch:

  • Net income diverging sharply from Underlying Profit in revaluation years
  • The gap between Underlying and Recurring Underlying — one-off gains inflating the headline non-GAAP number too

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: Sum-of-the-parts: owner-FCF DCF of the consolidated operating businesses, plus listed stakes in Swire Properties and Cathay Pacific at market, less holdco net debt and NCI. A 35% holding-company discount is then applied to the undiscounted SOTP NAV (-HK$57,481m, -HK$8.52/B share, the same in every scenario), anchored on the 10-year P/B ceiling of 0.40x — the richest multiple the market has paid for the B shares against book, versus an undiscounted SOTP of about 0.62x book. The 10-year average P/B (0.30x) is deliberately not used: part of that historical gap is Swire Properties' own discount to its NAV, already captured by marking SP at market, so averaging would double-count it. This drops the weighted intrinsic value from HK$24.38 to HK$15.86 per B share; the operating DCF (8% WACC), stake marks and scenario weights are unchanged.
